name: salamander
about: Chain ragdoll body for the giant salamander (31-bone quadruped rig, shared with the eel and elephant). 13 capsules: hips (root, spine0), chest, head (with neck), tail_a, tail_b, and 4 legs x (upper, lower). Bones without a body (spine1, spine3, spine4, ears, jaw, pasterns, paws, tail1, tail3) follow their parent bone in the scene graph. Every number is here; src/chain.mjs holds none.
placeholder_note: radii, masses, joint limits and motor scales are PLACEHOLDERS to tune on Dom's phone and the clips; only the bone positions are measured.
scale_source: Armagedom model scale x3.6 (Dom's recon note 2026-10-28): bones and radii below are in model units, the row is in metres at this scale
mass_assumption: placeholder: the Chinese giant salamander reaches about 1.8 m and 50-65 kg; this one is about 3.6 m long at x3.6, so about 8x the volume of a 1.8 m one would be 400+ kg; 280 kg total is a squat estimate for a thin-bodied amphibian. Tune against how heavy the fall should feel.
inertia_source: data/ragdoll-role-table.json motor.inertia_multiplier (M1 finding), same value as the humanoid rows
hinge_flex_z_source: own: the creature faces +z. A hind knee flexes the lower leg backward (-z, like a human knee); a front elbow flexes it forward (+z, like a human elbow). Row-level so the engine does not need the humanoid 'shin' role.

segments.source: placeholder: spine2 to neck (spine3, spine4 ride on it)
placeholder: neck to jaw (neck + head + jaw, ears ride on it)
placeholder: tail2 to tail3 plus 0.05 model units past the last bone
